page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% scores in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests all falling within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the overall PassMark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the ecs.se1.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and medium-scale multi-threaded processing tasks.
